literal: Evil things evil yielding-because, evil things fire-than-even to-fear will-be.
translation: Because evil deeds yield only evil, they are to be feared even more than fire.
modern: தீய செயல்கள் தீமையான விளைவுகளையே தருவதால், அத்தீய செயல்களை நெருப்பை விட அதிகமாகப் பயந்து ஒதுக்க வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet explains why one should be terrified of committing evil deeds. The word 'தீயவை' refers to bad actions, which inherently produce 'தீய' or bad outcomes, indicated by 'பயத்தலால்' (because they yield). Because their result is always harmful, the poet compares them to fire ('தீ'). However, evil deeds are said to be feared ('அஞ்சப்படும்') even more than fire, as fire only burns what it touches, while evil deeds bring lasting ruin.
